Fish Fillet
time Instant

Fish are animals found in the fishing lake. They produce fish fillets.

They are unlocked at experience level 27 when players can repair the fishing boat and go to the lake.

Catching fish

Main article: Fishing

Fish can be caught using lures crafted from the Lure Workbench and fishing nets and mystery nets made in the Net Maker.

Players can catch all different species of fish when fishing with lures but only three when fishing with nets (i.e. species which can otherwise be caught with red lures).

Catching a fish with a lure is instantaneous. Catching fish with a net takes 20 or 21 hours.

Six fish can only be caught during special fishing events: Carps, Giant Barbs, Lake Sturgeons, Nile Perches, Red-Tailed Catfish, and Zanders.

Fishing book

Main article: Fishing Book

Fish players have already caught can be found in the fishing book, which opens by tapping on the fishing hut.


Fish Weight

Upon catching a fish you are awarded a grade based on its weight. The heavier the fish, the higher the grade. The four grades are as follows: Bronze, Silver, Gold, and Platinum. Catching a fish always yields one fillet regardless of weight.

There is a large variation in the weight of a fish, ranging from 1 lb to 17 lbs. Certain fish species are more likely to be heavier than others. For example, Sockeye Salmon have a maximum weight of 5.3 lbs. Huchen have a maximum weight of 3 lbs. Using Boosters will increase the maximum weight of a fish.

Fish weight is important for Fishing Derby tasks which require a total number of pounds or kilograms to be caught. Fish weight is also important for completing the Fishing Book, which requires you catch a Bronze, Silver, Gold, and Platinum fish to acquire all the diamonds in the book. Before reeling in a specific fish it is impossible to tell how heavy the fish will be. The Circle Size and Pull does not correlate to the weight when the fish is caught. Weight is randomly assigned when the fish is caught and based on the weight distribution shown in the table below:

Fish Weight
Booster Bronze Silver Gold Platinum
None 49.9% 37.1% 10.2% 2.8%
10% 17.6% 38.3% 22.6% 21.5%
25% 1.7% 11.8% 17.8% 68.70%
40% 0% 1.6% 4.7% 93.7%

Fish species

There are dozens of different fish species in the game. Each can be caught with one or two kinds of lures. While most fish can be caught in any spot, some do not and all fish have a favorite spot.

Here is a map of all the spots:

If you need to catch a specific fish, you must pay attention to 4 different criteria:

  1. Fishing Spot - Certain fish not only prefer, but are exclusive to specific spots. For example, it is impossible to find a Goldfish anywhere but spot 11.
  2. Lure Type - Fish species can be caught with one or two lure colors and no others. For example, you cannot catch a Largemouth Bass with anything but a Green Lure.
  3. Circle Size - Once a fish has been hooked, a reticle (circle) will appear as part of the minigame. Every fish species has a specific circle size. The 3 sizes are Small, Medium, and Large. A special fourth size (Event) is specific for Event Fish. If you are looking for a specific fish it is important you release the fish if it does not correspond to the correct circle size.
  4. Pull (weight) - Once a fish has been hooked, its response to "reeling" is also fish specific. This is correlated with the average weight of the species. Fish are either "Heavy", and difficult to pull or "Light", and can be pulled easily. This is best highlighted in the difference between a Sockeye Salmon (Heavy) and a Huchen or Copper Redhorse (Light).

The following table displays each type of fish and its 4 specific criteria required to catch it.

Note: spot data is based on users' experiences and may be erroneous.
Note: for more detailed information see Fishing List.

Fish weight distribution and weight classes

The infographic above summaries the weight distribution from catching 1,000 sockeye salmon.  The bottom section gives players an idea of how many sockeye salmon they need to catch to clear a 320 point derby fishing task, with and without the use of fishing weight boosters.

There are a few videos on YouTube demonstrating how a player can identify a sockeye salmon vs a huchen or copper redhorse when using a red lure.  The same swimming profile of the sockeye salmon is shared with 10 other fish that chase voucher lures (in case you are all out of red lures), and two other voucher fish (coho salmon and goldfish) move half the speed of the sockeye salmon, so there are 12 other fish a player can target with the voucher lures while fishing efficiently for a derby task.
